fmt_phone: Whenever the text contains exactly 11 digits (not counting any extension) and the first digit is 1, it drops that leading 1 and formats the remaining 10 digits as (AAA) BBB-CCCC (so '+1 555 123 4567' and '15551234567' both give '(555) 123-4567'). Any extension is removed and added at the end as ' x' followed by its digits, so '1 415 555 0132 ext 12' gives '(415) 555-0132 x12'.

fmt_phone: Whenever the text contains at least one digit but does not end up with exactly 10 digits (after dropping a single leading 1 from 11 digits, and not counting any extension), it returns an empty string instead of the original text. This covers 11 digits that do not start with 1 (such as '2 555 123 4567'), fewer than 10 digits (such as a seven-digit number with no area code like '555-0132'), 12 or more digits, and an international number like '+44 20 7946 0958'. An extension such as 'ext 89' or 'ext 12' is never counted as part of the 10 digits: it is taken out before counting, and when the number itself is valid it is appended to the formatted number as ' x89' (or ' x12'). When the number itself is not valid, the extension is dropped along with it and the result is an empty string. Text with no digits at all is handled by the no-digits rule instead.

fmt_phone: Whenever letters or other words are mixed in with exactly 10 digits (such as 'CALL-555-123-4567'), the non-digit characters are thrown away and the number is formatted; but a vanity number with letters instead of digits ('1-800-FLOWERS') has too few digits and, like any other text with fewer than 10 digits, returns an empty string.

fmt_phone: Whenever the area code or exchange begins with 0 or 1 (such as '0551234567'), it is still formatted as-is ('(055) 123-4567'); no check is made that the number is a valid North American number. Only a single leading 1 on an 11-digit number is removed.
fmt_phone: Whenever the input is NULL, it returns NULL; whenever it is empty text, it returns empty text; whenever it has no digits ('abc'), it returns the text unchanged.

fmt_phone: Whenever the input is a plain number rather than text (such as 5551234567 or 15551234567), it is treated as its digits and formatted by the same rules as text. A decimal number such as 5551234567.0 has an extra digit, which makes 11 digits not starting with 1, so it returns an empty string, not the original number. Any number that does not end up with exactly 10 digits (after dropping a single leading 1 from 11 digits) returns an empty string.
fmt_phone: Whenever the digits are written in non-Western numerals (such as Arabic-Indic digits), they are not recognised as digits and the text is returned unchanged.

grade_letter: Whenever the score is above 100 or below 0 it returns 'X', and this check comes first, before any grade is looked at, so extra credit or any other reason does not lift a score above 100 into a grade. Otherwise, whenever the score is 92 or more (up to and including 100) it returns 'A'; 83 or more but under 92 returns 'B'; 71 or more but under 83 returns 'C'; 60 or more but under 71 returns 'D'; anything lower (down to 0) returns 'F'.

grade_letter: Whenever the score is exactly on a grade cut-off (92, 83, 71, 60) it gets the higher grade: exactly 92 is an 'A', exactly 83 is a 'B', exactly 71 is a 'C', exactly 60 is a 'D'. A score of exactly 90 is not on a cut-off and is a 'B'. Scores are never rounded, so 91.99 or 91.9999999 is a 'B', 89.99 is a 'B', and 59.99 is an 'F'.

grade_letter: Whenever the score is above 100 or below 0 it returns 'X'. Scores above 100 are not accepted, so 100.01 and 105 both return 'X', even with extra credit. Exactly 0 is valid and returns 'F'. Exactly 100 is valid and returns 'A'.
grade_letter: Whenever the score is NULL, it returns NULL.
grade_letter: Whenever the score is text holding a number ('95', ' 85 ', '89.5', '1e2'), it is read as that number; text that starts with a number ('85%', '90abc') uses the leading number.

grade_letter: Whenever the score is not a number, it returns NULL rather than 'F'. This covers empty or blank text, text with no leading number ('abc', 'A', '-', '0x5A'), and the boolean true. None of these is treated as 0. Text that does hold a number or starts with one is still read as a number under rule 23, and a real score of 0 still returns 'F'.

late_fee: Whenever an invoice is late, the days late are first rounded down to a whole number of days (any part-day is dropped). After that, the first 5 days late are free, so only the days beyond the 5th are charged. An invoice late by 5 whole days or fewer has no fee. For each charged day the fee is 0.5% of the invoice amount in cents, and the total is rounded down to a whole number of cents. The fee has a minimum of 500 cents, and it is capped at 20% of the invoice amount in cents, rounded down. The cap wins over the minimum, so on a small invoice where 20% of the invoice is less than 500 cents, the fee is that 20% amount. Example: 10000 cents, 10 days late: 5 charged days give 250, raised to the 500 minimum, so the fee is 500. The cap here is 2000.

late_fee: Whenever the fee for the charged days (the days beyond the first 5 free days) is not a whole number of cents, it is rounded to the nearest cent with exact halves rounded up. Days within the first 5 are never charged, so an invoice late by 5 days or fewer has a fee of 0, with no rounding up and no minimum. Examples of the rounding: 100 cents for 8 days (3 charged days) gives 1.5, which rounds to 2; 1 cent for 100 days (95 charged days) gives 0.475, which rounds to 0; 1 cent for 99 days gives 0.47, which rounds to 0; 99 cents for 10 days (5 charged days) gives 2.475, which rounds to 2 (before the minimum and cap in rule 25 are applied); 100 cents for 1 day, or for 3 days, gives 0 because those days are free.
late_fee: Whenever days late is zero or negative (not late), or the invoice amount is zero or negative, the fee is 0.
late_fee: Whenever either the amount or the days late is NULL, it returns NULL.

late_fee: Whenever days late is a fraction (such as 6.5 or 2.5), it is first rounded down to a whole number of days, and only then are the first 5 days treated as free and the days beyond them charged (10000 cents for 6.5 days counts as 6 days, so 1 charged day, which gives 50, raised to the 500 minimum, so the fee is 500). A fractional days late that rounds down to 5 or less (such as 1.5, 2.5 or 5.9) is entirely within the free days, so the fee is 0 (10000 cents for 2.5 days gives 0). A fractional amount (1000.5) is still used as is before the final rounding to a whole cent.

late_fee: Whenever the amount or days late is text, a number in the text is used ('10000' and '10' give 500; '3 days' counts as 3); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so the fee is 0 and not NULL.

shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is valid and is not over 30000 g (30 kg), the charge is zone x (300 + 100 x the number of started kilograms) cents, where any part of a kilogram counts as a whole one (500 g in zone 1 gives 400; exactly 1000 g gives 400; 1001 g gives 500; 2500 g in zone 2 gives 1200). The zone used here is the zone the parcel is billed as under rule 34, so a parcel whose zone is 0, negative, not a whole number, not a number at all, or above 3 is still priced, as zone 3, and never returns NULL because of its zone (for example, 500 g in zone 0 gives 1200, the same as zone 3). A weight over 30000 g is not priced by this formula, because it gets the flat charge in rule 37.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is exactly 0, the charge is the base amount only: zone x 300 cents (zone 3 gives 900), and the fractional weight 0.5 g counts as one started kilogram.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is negative, it returns NULL.

shipping_cost: A zone that is not a number at all (empty text, 'abc', 'A'), is not a whole number (1.5), or is outside 1 to 3 (below 1, meaning zero or negative, or above 3) is billed as zone 3, and it does not return NULL. A whole-valued zone like 2.0 or '1.0' is accepted as that zone number. There is no zone above 3, so zone 100 is billed as zone 3.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight or zone is NULL, it returns NULL.

shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is text, a number in the text is used ('500', '2kg' counts as 2 g); empty text or text with no leading number counts as a weight of 0 (charged only the base amount), while text with a leading number in the zone ('2z' is zone 2) is accepted.

shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is over 30000 g (30 kg), there is no per-kilogram pricing and no weight is too large for this rule: the charge is a flat 9999 cents, whatever the zone, including a zone billed as zone 3 under rule 34, and however the weight was given (for example, 1,000,000,000 g in zone 1 gives 9999, and a 100 kg pallet, which is 100000 g, to zone 3 gives 9999, not 30900). A weight of exactly 30000 g is priced normally under rule 31.
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is under 10, the total is the unit price times the quantity with no discount (250 cents x 5 gives 1250).

tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is 10 to 49 units, the whole order, not just the units above 10, gets 10% off (250 x 10 gives 2250; 250 x 11 gives 2475), so 10 units can cost the same as 9 units (2250 each). Whenever the quantity is 50 or more, the whole order gets 20% off.

tiered_price: The total is rounded to the nearest 5 cents, with exact halves rounded up, so the total is always a multiple of 5 cents (1 cent x 10 gives 10; 1 cent x 15 gives 15; 1 cent x 25 gives 25; 99.5 cents x 3 gives 300).
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is 0 or the unit price is 0, the total is 0.
tiered_price: Whenever the unit price is negative, it returns NULL. Whenever the quantity is negative (and the unit price is not negative), the total is 0, not NULL (minus 2 items at 10.00 gives 0).
tiered_price: Whenever either the unit price or quantity is NULL, it returns NULL.
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is a fraction, it is used as is and the discount applies only when it is 10 or more (9.99 gives no discount, 250 x 9.99 gives 2498; 10.0 gets the discount).

tiered_price: Whenever the price or quantity is text, a number in the text is used ('250' and '10' give 2250; '12x' counts as 12); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so the total is 0 and not NULL.

weighted_rating: Whenever the rating and the number of votes are valid, the result is (votes x average rating + 30) / (votes + 10), that is the average pulled toward a neutral prior of 3.0 that is worth 10 votes (5.0 with 10 votes gives 4.0; 4.5 with 100 votes gives 4.36).
weighted_rating: Whenever the result is calculated, it is rounded to 2 decimal places with exact halves rounded up, and is returned as a decimal number (4.0, not 4).
weighted_rating: Whenever there are fewer than 5 votes, including 0 votes, the result is NULL. Exactly 5 votes is accepted.
weighted_rating: Whenever the votes are negative, it returns NULL; whenever either the rating or the votes are NULL, it returns NULL.

weighted_rating: Whenever the average rating lies outside any normal scale (0, negative or above 5, such as -2 or 7), it is not rejected or limited and is used as given (rating 0 with 10 votes gives 1.5; rating 7 with 10 votes gives 5.0).
weighted_rating: Whenever the votes are a fraction (2.5), they are used as is in the calculation.

weighted_rating: Whenever the rating or votes are text, a number in the text is used ('5' and '10' give 4.0); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so a rating of 'abc' counts as rating 0 (giving 1.5 with 10 votes) and votes of 'abc' counts as 0 votes, which is fewer than 5 votes, so the result is NULL, not 3.0.
gross_receipts: Whenever a group of rows is totalled, it adds up only the amounts that are greater than zero; negative amounts (refunds) are left out and not subtracted (100, -50, 300 gives 400).
gross_receipts: Whenever an amount is NULL or exactly 0, it adds nothing to the total.

gross_receipts: Whenever there are no rows, only NULL amounts, or only zero or negative amounts (that is, no valid rows with an amount greater than zero), the total is NULL, not 0. Whenever at least one amount greater than zero is counted, the total is the sum of those amounts.

gross_receipts: Whenever every counted amount is a whole number, the total is a whole number; whenever any counted amount has decimals the total is a decimal number (100.5 and 200 give 300.5), using ordinary floating point addition (0.1 and 0.2 give 0.30000000000000004).

gross_receipts: Whenever amounts are text, a number in the text is used ('100' and '250.5' give 350.5; '12x' counts as 12; '1e2' counts as 100.0); text with no leading number counts as 0 and adds nothing.

gross_receipts: Whenever it is used with GROUP BY, each group is totalled separately by the same rules (a group with only refunds, only zero or NULL amounts, or no valid rows gives NULL, not 0), and rows removed by WHERE are not counted.
gross_receipts: Whenever DISTINCT is written inside it, it is ignored and every row is still added (amounts 5, 5, 3 give 13, not 8).

slugify: Whenever a title is given, it returns the text in lower case with every run of characters that are not letters a-z or digits 0-9 (spaces, punctuation, tabs, line breaks, underscores, symbols) replaced by one single dash ('Hello, World!' gives 'hello-world'; 'snake_case' gives 'snake-case').
slugify: Whenever the result would begin or end with a dash (leading or trailing spaces or punctuation, such as '  Hello   World  ' or '--Hello--'), those dashes are removed.

slugify: Whenever the title has accented letters, they are reduced to the plain letter ('Café Crème Brûlée' gives 'cafe-creme-brulee'; 'Ça va' gives 'ca-va'), and full-width letters and digits, ligatures and superscripts are also converted to plain ones ('ﬁne' gives 'fine', 'x²' gives 'x2').

slugify: Whenever a letter has no plain-letter form (ß, Æ, Ø, and all non-Latin scripts such as Japanese, and emoji), it is silently deleted rather than turned into a dash or transliterated ('Straße' gives 'strae'; 'Ærø Øl ß' gives 'r-l'; '日本語 Tokyo' gives 'tokyo').

slugify: Whenever the title has typographic dashes or quotes (en dash, em dash, curly quotes), they are deleted and not turned into a dash, so the words either side are joined ('a–b—c' gives 'abc'). A plain apostrophe is also deleted, not turned into a dash ('dog's' gives 'dogs').

slugify: Whenever the finished web address would come out empty for any reason, it returns 'untitled', not NULL and not empty text. This covers a title that is empty, spaces only, made only of punctuation or symbols ('!!!'), made only of characters that are deleted (non-Latin characters, emoji, typographic dashes and quotes, apostrophes), or any mix of these, such as '?? 日本語 !!'. The check is made after all the other steps (lower-casing, dash replacement, accent reduction, deletions and removal of leading and trailing dashes), so a title with no letters or digits always gives 'untitled'.
slugify: Whenever the title is NULL, it returns NULL.
slugify: Whenever the input is a number (12345 or 12.5), it is treated as its text and a decimal point becomes a dash ('12-5').

mask_card: Whenever a card number has 13 or more digits, it returns one '*' for every digit except the last 4, followed by those last 4 digits ('4111111111111111' gives '************1111'), so the number of digits and stars is unchanged. Spaces and hyphens in the number are not digits and are not removed (see the rule on spaces and hyphens).

mask_card: Spaces and hyphens in the number stay exactly where they are, and the digits are masked as before, so that only the last four digits are shown and every other digit is replaced with '*' ('4111 1111 1111 1111' gives '**** **** **** 1111'; '4111-1111-1111-1111' gives '****-****-****-1111'). Any other non-digit character, such as dots, slashes, underscores or brackets, makes it return 'INVALID'.

mask_card: Whenever the number has fewer than 13 digits, it returns 'INVALID' instead of a masked number, because it is too short to be a card number ('1234' gives 'INVALID'; '123' gives 'INVALID'; '411' gives 'INVALID'; '0000' gives 'INVALID'). Exactly 13 digits is long enough and is masked as usual.

mask_card: Whenever the input has no digits at all (empty text, or text with only letters such as 'abcd' or whatever else a cashier types instead of a card number), it returns the text 'INVALID', never an empty string and never a mask, because zero digits is fewer than 13 digits.
mask_card: Whenever the input is NULL, it returns NULL.

mask_card: Whenever the input has letters or other text mixed with digits, only the digits count, and the last 4 digits found are shown even if they come from other text ('4111 1111 1111 1111 exp 12/26' gives '****************1226'). If the digits found number fewer than 13, it returns 'INVALID' ('XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-1111' gives 'INVALID', because the X's and any existing '*' are dropped and only 4 digits remain).

mask_card: Whenever the input is a plain number rather than text (4111111111111111), it is treated as its digits and masked in the same way; a number with a decimal point such as 41.5 counts its digits and not the point (3 digits, which is fewer than 13, so it gives 'INVALID').
mask_card: Whenever digits are written in non-Western numerals (such as Arabic-Indic digits), they are counted as digits and the last four are shown as written.

biz_days_between: Whenever the period contains only Saturdays and Sundays, it returns 0; a weekend start day is not counted but a weekend end day is simply excluded like any end day.

late_fee: Whenever days late is zero or negative (not late), or the invoice amount is zero or negative, the fee is 0.
late_fee: Whenever either the amount or the days late is NULL, it returns NULL.

Whenever days late is a fraction (such as 1.5) it is used as is in the calculation, and the first 5 days late are still free, so a fractional number of days late of 5 or less gives a fee of 0 (10000 cents for 1.5 days gives 0). Beyond 5 days, only the days past the 5th, including any fraction, are charged (10000 cents for 5.5 days charges 0.5 days, which gives 25, raised to the 500 minimum, so the fee is 500). A fractional amount (1000.5) is used as is before the final rounding to a whole cent.

late_fee: Whenever the amount or days late is text, a number in the text is used ('10000' and '10' give 500; '3 days' counts as 3); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so the fee is 0 and not NULL.

shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is valid, the parcel is always priced and never left blank because of its zone. For a weight of 30000 g (30 kg) or less, the charge is the billed zone x (300 + 100 x the number of started kilograms) cents, where any part of a kilogram counts as a whole one (500 g in zone 1 gives 400; exactly 1000 g gives 400; 1001 g gives 500; 2500 g in zone 2 gives 1200). A weight over 30000 g (30 kg) is not priced this way: it is a flat 9999 cents (99.99 dollars) whatever the zone, and there is no other weight limit or cap (see rule 37). The billed zone is the zone given if it is a valid zone, and zone 3 otherwise (see rule 34). Any zone that is not a valid zone is billed as zone 3, whether it is out of range, zero, or not a whole number. So 500 g in zone 99 is billed as zone 3 and gives 1200 cents (12 dollars), 500 g in zone 2.5 gives 1200 cents, and 500 g in zone 0 gives 1200 cents.

Whenever the weight is exactly 0, the charge is the base amount only: billed zone x 300 cents (zone 3 gives 900), and the fractional weight 0.5 g counts as one started kilogram. The billed zone is worked out as in rule 34, so an invalid zone such as 2.5 or 0 is billed as zone 3 and gives 900, not a blank.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is negative, it returns NULL.

A zone that is not a number at all (empty text, 'abc', 'A'), is not a whole number (1.5, 2.5), or is outside 1 to 3 (below 1, meaning zero or negative, or above 3) is invalid. An invalid zone is billed as zone 3, never by multiplying by the number given, and it never leaves the charge blank (it does not return NULL). So a zone of 2.5 or 0 is billed as zone 3, and 500 g in zone 2.5 or zone 0 gives 1200 cents (12 dollars). This holds for any valid weight, including a weight of exactly 0. A whole-valued zone like 2.0 or '1.0' is accepted as that zone number. There is no zone above 3, so any zone above 3 (such as 99 or 100) is billed as zone 3; for example 500 g in zone 99 gives 1200 cents (12 dollars). Only a zone that is NULL gives NULL (see rule 35).
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight or zone is NULL, it returns NULL.

shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is text, a number in the text is used ('500', '2kg' counts as 2 g); empty text or text with no leading number counts as a weight of 0 (charged only the base amount), while text with a leading number in the zone ('2z' is zone 2) is accepted.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is over 30000 g, the charge is a flat 9999, whatever the zone (for example, 1,000,000,000 g in zone 1 gives 9999). A weight of exactly 30000 g is priced normally.
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is under 10, the total is the unit price times the quantity with no discount (250 cents x 5 gives 1250).

tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is 10 to 49 units, the whole order, not just the units above 10, gets 10% off (250 x 10 gives 2250; 250 x 11 gives 2475), so 10 units can cost the same as 9 units (2250 each). Whenever the quantity is 50 or more, the whole order, not just the units above 50, gets 20% off instead of 10%, and this holds however large the quantity is (1000 items at 1000 cents each is 1000000 cents less 20%, which gives 800000 cents, or 8000 dollars). There are two discount levels, 10% and 20%, and the 10% level does not apply at 50 or more.

tiered_price: Every total, after any discount, is rounded to the nearest 5 cents, with exact halves rounded up. The total is never left in exact cents, so it is always a multiple of 5 cents (1 cent x 10 gives 10; 1 cent x 15 gives 15; 1 cent x 25 gives 25; 99.5 cents x 3 gives 300). This applies to every price and quantity. For example, 10 items at 333 cents is 3330 less 10%, which is 2997 cents, and that is rounded to a 5-cent multiple, not kept as 2997.
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is 0 or the unit price is 0, the total is 0.

tiered_price: Whenever the unit price is negative, it returns NULL. Whenever the quantity is 0 or less (negative quantities, including fractions and text numbers such as '-3', are covered), the total is 0, not NULL, so a return keyed in as an order of minus 3 items gives 0. This holds even when no unit price is given (the unit price is missing/NULL): a quantity of 0 or less still gives 0, not blank. A negative unit price still gives NULL, including when the quantity is also negative.

tiered_price: Whenever either the unit price or quantity is NULL, it returns NULL, except when the quantity is 0 or less: then the total is 0 even if the unit price is NULL (a missing price does not turn a zero or negative quantity into a blank total). A NULL quantity still returns NULL.
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is a fraction, it is used as is and the discount applies only when it is 10 or more (9.99 gives no discount, 250 x 9.99 gives 2498; 10.0 gets the discount).

tiered_price: Whenever the price or quantity is text, a number in the text is used ('250' and '10' give 2250; '12x' counts as 12); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so the total is 0 and not NULL.

weighted_rating: Whenever the rating and the number of votes are valid and there are at least 5 votes, the result is (votes x average rating + 30) / (votes + 10), that is the average pulled toward a neutral prior of 3.0 that is worth 10 votes (5.0 with 10 votes gives 4.0; 4.5 with 100 votes gives 4.36). With fewer than 5 votes there is no result, only NULL (see rule 48).
weighted_rating: Whenever the result is calculated, it is rounded to 2 decimal places with exact halves rounded up, and is returned as a decimal number (4.0, not 4).
weighted_rating: Whenever there are fewer than 5 votes, including 0 votes, the result is NULL. Exactly 5 votes is accepted.
weighted_rating: Whenever the votes are negative, it returns NULL; whenever either the rating or the votes are NULL, it returns NULL.

weighted_rating: Whenever the average rating lies outside any normal scale (0, negative or above 5, such as -2 or 7), it is not rejected or limited and is used as given (rating 0 with 10 votes gives 1.5; rating 7 with 10 votes gives 5.0).
weighted_rating: Whenever the votes are a fraction (2.5), they are used as is in the calculation.

weighted_rating: Whenever the rating or votes are text, a number in the text is used ('5' and '10' give 4.0); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so a rating of 'abc' counts as rating 0 (giving 1.5 with 10 votes) and votes of 'abc' counts as 0 votes, which is fewer than 5 votes, so the result is NULL.
gross_receipts: Whenever a group of rows is totalled, it adds up only the amounts that are greater than zero; negative amounts (refunds) are left out and not subtracted (100, -50, 300 gives 400).
gross_receipts: Whenever an amount is NULL or exactly 0, it adds nothing to the total.

gross_receipts: Whenever there are no valid rows, the total is NULL, not 0. That covers no rows at all, only NULL amounts, only zero or negative amounts, and only text that is skipped under the text rule. A valid row is one whose amount is actually added to the total. If at least one amount is added, the total is the sum of the added amounts.

gross_receipts: Whenever every counted amount is a whole number, the total is a whole number; whenever any counted amount has decimals the total is a decimal number (100.5 and 200 give 300.5), using ordinary floating point addition (0.1 and 0.2 give 0.30000000000000004).

gross_receipts: Whenever amounts are text, the text is used only if the whole text is a number ('100' and '250.5' give 350.5; '1e2' counts as 100.0). Text that is not entirely a number is skipped and adds nothing, whether it has no leading number or a number followed by other characters ('12abc' and '12x' are skipped, not counted as 12; so '12abc' next to 10 gives 10).

gross_receipts: Whenever it is used with GROUP BY, each group is totalled separately by the same rules (a group with only refunds, or with no valid rows, gives NULL), and rows removed by WHERE are not counted.
gross_receipts: Whenever DISTINCT is written inside it, it is ignored and every row is still added (amounts 5, 5, 3 give 13, not 8).

slugify: Whenever a title is given, it returns the text in lower case. Every ampersand (&) becomes the word 'and', set apart from the words around it by dashes, even when it has no spaces around it ('Rock & Roll' gives 'rock-and-roll'; 'R&D' gives 'r-and-d'). Every run of the other characters that are not letters a-z or digits 0-9 (spaces, punctuation, tabs, line breaks, underscores, symbols) is replaced by one single dash ('Hello, World!' gives 'hello-world'; 'snake_case' gives 'snake-case'). Dashes next to the word 'and' that come from an ampersand merge with any neighbouring dashes into one.
slugify: Whenever the result would begin or end with a dash (leading or trailing spaces or punctuation, such as '  Hello   World  ' or '--Hello--'), those dashes are removed.

slugify: Whenever the title has accented letters, they are reduced to the plain letter ('Café Crème Brûlée' gives 'cafe-creme-brulee'; 'Ça va' gives 'ca-va'), and full-width letters and digits, ligatures and superscripts are also converted to plain ones ('ﬁne' gives 'fine', 'x²' gives 'x2').

slugify: Whenever a letter has no plain-letter form (ß, Æ, Ø, and all non-Latin scripts such as Japanese, and emoji), it is silently deleted rather than turned into a dash or transliterated ('Straße' gives 'strae'; 'Ærø Øl ß' gives 'r-l'; '日本語 Tokyo' gives 'tokyo').

slugify: Whenever the title has typographic dashes or quotes (en dash, em dash, curly quotes), they are deleted and not turned into a dash, so the words either side are joined ('a–b—c' gives 'abc'). A plain apostrophe is also deleted, not turned into a dash ('dog's' gives 'dogs').

slugify: Whenever the result would be empty once everything is done (every character that is not a plain letter or digit has been turned into dashes or deleted, and leading and trailing dashes removed), it returns 'untitled', not NULL and not empty text. This covers an empty title, spaces only, '!!!', titles made only of characters that get deleted (non-Latin scripts such as '日本語', emoji, ß, Æ, Ø, typographic dashes or quotes, apostrophes), and any mix of these. An ampersand is not deleted but becomes 'and', so a title of just '&' gives 'and', not 'untitled'.
slugify: Whenever the title is NULL, it returns NULL.
slugify: Whenever the input is a number (12345 or 12.5), it is treated as its text and a decimal point becomes a dash ('12-5').

mask_card: Whenever a card number has 13 or more digits, it returns one '*' for every digit except the last 4, followed by those last 4 digits, with any spaces staying exactly where they were in the number ('4111111111111111' gives '************1111', and '4111 1111 1111 1111' gives '**** **** **** 1111'). The one exception is an American Express card, which is a number of exactly 15 digits that starts with 34 or 37: it keeps the last 5 digits visible and masks every digit before them with '*', so it shows ten stars and then the last 5 digits ('378282246310005' gives '**********10005'). The digits in the result are as many as the digits in the number; spaces are kept in their places and are not removed or regrouped.

mask_card: Spaces and hyphens in the number stay exactly where they are, and the digits are masked as before, so that only the last four digits are shown (the last five for an American Express card, as in the rule above) and every other digit is replaced with '*' ('4111-1111-1111-1111' gives '****-****-****-1111'). Any other non-digit character, such as dots, slashes, underscores or brackets, makes it return 'INVALID'.

mask_card: Whenever the number has fewer than 13 digits (but at least one), it returns 'INVALID' and nothing is masked or shown. This holds however few digits there are, including a number of only 4 digits, which is never masked to '****' ('1234', '123', '0000' and '4111-1111' all give 'INVALID'). Only a number with 13 or more digits is masked.

mask_card: Whenever the input has no digits at all, it returns 'INVALID' and never an empty result, because zero digits is fewer than 13. This covers empty text, text made only of letters such as 'abc' or 'abcd', text made only of spaces, hyphens or other characters, and anything else that is not a card number.
mask_card: Whenever the input is NULL, it returns NULL.

mask_card: Whenever the input has letters or other text mixed with digits, only the digits count, and the last 4 digits found are shown even if they come from other text, provided at least 13 digits are found ('4111 1111 1111 1111 exp 12/26' gives '****************1226'). The American Express rule applies to the digits found: if exactly 15 digits are found and they start with 34 or 37, the last 5 are shown instead. The X's and any existing '*' are dropped and not counted, so if fewer than 13 digits remain the result is 'INVALID' ('XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-1111' has only 4 digits and gives 'INVALID').

mask_card: Whenever the input is a plain number rather than text (4111111111111111), it is treated as its digits and handled in the same way, including the 13-digit minimum; a number with a decimal point such as 41.5 counts its digits and not the point, so its 3 digits are fewer than 13 and it gives 'INVALID'.

mask_card: Whenever digits are written in non-Western numerals (such as Arabic-Indic digits), they are counted as digits and the last four are shown as written (the last five for an American Express card: exactly 15 digits starting with 34 or 37).
Nothing else. Enter

A shop with no votes at all: it shows a middle 3.0 stars rather than no rating. The owner says: No, with fewer than 5 votes the rating isn't trusted yet, so it should be NULL, not 3.0.
